title: Keeper App Part 1 Solution
summary: Builds Keeper App Part 1 step by step: an App root component in a components folder, then Header, Footer (with a computed year) and Note components. The main lessons are that the provided CSS only applies when JSX uses the exact elements it targets, and that attributes such as className must go on HTML elements inside a component, not on the custom component tag.

concepts.heading: Start small and verify
points: Begin with index.js rendering a plain <h1> into #root to prove the setup works before adding components.
Then swap that h1 for <App /> once App exists; seeing App's own placeholder text (e.g. 'Hello App') confirms the import and render are wired correctly.

concepts.heading: .jsx vs .js file extensions
points: The challenge names files with .jsx. The Airbnb React style guide recommends .jsx so tools like Bitbucket or Atlassian products can recognise and highlight JSX syntax.
Functionally React does not care: components work fine in .js files. This is a style choice, and the lecture notes that many developers (including the instructor) now drop the x.
Rule: choose one convention for a project and use it consistently.
(Extra) Vite-based projects (like the reference repo) do care: Vite expects JSX to live in .jsx files by default, so keep the x there.

concepts.heading: Component file boilerplate
points: Keep components in a src/components folder. In this lecture App.jsx also lives there, so index.js imports it with import App from "./components/App" (extension omitted).
Every component file follows the same three steps: import React from "react"; define a function named in PascalCase that returns JSX; export default that function.
Use a default export because each file contains just one component.
Inside App, sibling component files are imported with a relative path from the same folder, e.g. import Header from "./Header".

(Extra) The import path's casing should match the file name exactly (./Header for Header.jsx). Some file systems are case-insensitive and let a mismatch slide locally, but Linux build servers will fail.

concepts.heading: Lowercase HTML elements vs PascalCase components
points: In JSX, lowercase tags (<header>, <footer>, <div>) are native HTML elements; capitalised tags (<Header />, <Footer />) are your own components.
That capitalisation is how React tells the two apart, so a component named header would be treated as an HTML tag.
Custom components with no children are written as self-closing tags: <Header />.
(Extra) The App in the reference repo returns a fragment (<>...</>) instead of a wrapping <div>. A fragment groups siblings without adding an extra DOM node; either satisfies JSX's single-root rule.

concepts.heading: Why the styling appears (or doesn't)
points: styles.css in the public folder uses element selectors: header gets the yellow background (#f5ba13), negative side margin, padding and a box-shadow; header h1 gets white text in the McLaren font.
So the Header looks right immediately only because it returns a real <header> containing an <h1>. If the styles don't show, the JSX isn't using the elements the CSS targets.

footer has position: absolute, bottom: 0, width: 100% and text-align: center; footer p sets the light grey colour. Returning just a

from Footer leaves the text unstyled at the top. It must be wrapped in a

element.

The note card uses a class selector (.note) plus descendant rules .note h1 and .note p, so the card only gets its white background, border-radius, box-shadow, padding, fixed 240px width and float: left once the wrapping div has that class.

concepts.heading: A dynamic copyright year
points: Avoid hard-coding a year that goes stale; some developers campaign against static footer years (the site updateyourfooter.com collects snippets for many languages).
new Date() creates a Date for the current moment; .getFullYear() returns the four-digit year as a number.
Either store it first (const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear();) and insert {currentYear}, or put the whole expression inline inside JSX curly braces.
The © symbol can be pasted in directly (copy it from a search result).

(Extra) Defining the year inside the component (as in the lecture) recalculates it on every render; defining it at module level (as in the reference repo) calculates it once when the file loads. Both give the right year for a normal page visit.

concepts.heading: HTML attributes belong on HTML elements
points: Writing <Note className="note" /> in App does nothing visible: the class never reaches the DOM.
Attributes like className, style or onClick only take effect on native elements. Put className="note" on the <div> that Note returns.
className is JSX's name for the HTML class attribute.
Why this happens is explained in the next lecture on props: anything written on a custom component tag is passed in as a prop, not applied as an HTML attribute.

pitfalls: Putting className (or style/onClick) on the custom component tag, e.g. <Note className="note" />. It is silently ignored; apply it to the div inside the component.

Writing the header text in a div instead of a <header> element, so the yellow bar never appears.
Naming a component in lowercase; React then treats it as an unknown HTML tag.
Hard-coding the year in the footer.
Mixing .js and .jsx conventions within one project.
